semantic_correction.stem: A client received a hazardous antineoplastic drug and remains within the facility's defined post-treatment excreta-precaution period. The nurse must handle urine-soiled linens. Which action is appropriate?

options.A: Wear two pairs of chemotherapy gloves and a disposable protective gown, adding eye and face protection if splashing is possible.
options.B: Wear one pair of standard examination gloves because hazardous-drug precautions end when the infusion is completed.
options.C: Handle the linens without protective clothing when the urine is not visibly bloody because drug exposure is no longer possible.
options.D: Shake the linens before bagging them so dried contamination is removed before they are sent for laundering.

semantic_correction.rationale: NIOSH identifies handling patient bodily waste and laundering or handling contaminated linens as occupational exposure pathways for hazardous antineoplastic drugs. In its antineoplastic-exposure case guidance, NIOSH recommends two pairs of protective chemotherapy gloves and a disposable gown when handling linens, urine, or feces from recently treated patients, with eye and face protection when splashing is possible. Current NIOSH hazardous-drug guidance emphasizes reducing worker exposure and using facility risk assessment and exposure controls appropriate to the drug and task. The stem already establishes that the client is within the facility-defined precaution period, so option A is the appropriate PPE response.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Use hazardous-drug PPE when handling excreta or contaminated linens from a client recently treated with an antineoplastic drug, following the facility's exposure-control plan.
semantic_correction.source_organization: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH), Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the 'only' distractor cue, shortened the uniquely long correct answer, and kept the post-treatment time window facility-defined while directly testing NIOSH-supported PPE for contaminated excreta/linens.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original answer was uniquely longest and one distractor used absolute wording. The revised item directly tests PPE for hazardous-drug-contaminated linens without imposing a universal excreta-precaution duration.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches NIOSH PPE recommendations for handling potentially contaminated urine or linens.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Hazardous-drug exposure can continue through bodily waste after administration and does not necessarily end with the infusion.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Antineoplastic drug exposure can occur through body fluids even when blood is not visible.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Shaking contaminated linens can increase dispersal and worker exposure rather than safely containing contamination.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone applies the NIOSH-recommended PPE to the task and the stem removes uncertainty about whether the facility's post-treatment precautions are still active.
cueing_check: All four choices are contaminated-linen handling actions of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
